node_definition.done_when: The plan sections the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot §3 (its stop-path paragraph and done-when, under the locked decision stale-snapshot-at-stop) and §11 are the authority; read both first. Stop path: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py --hook stop reads the same snapshot as the prompt path. A fresh snapshot refuses the stop exactly when it lists outstanding obligations. A snapshot that is not fresh, for any reason, imports the derivation lazily and derives inline under a production budget of 5 s that tests can override. It refuses the stop only when that result lists outstanding obligations, and allows the stop with one line naming the not-fresh reason when the budget runs out. Queued duty: in reckon/crew/obligations.py, a review duty whose most recent review attempt was refused as lane-paused (the attempt record that reckon/crew/recovery.py writes with status lane-paused; read it, do not change recovery.py) reads as review-queued within a stated bound. It names the refusal time and the session's published worker slots, is listed on the prompt path, and does not block the stop. Once the bound passes with no review dispatched, it returns to review-missing. The published snapshot carries the same reading, through reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py if needed. Two rendering fixes in the same files: not_fresh_line handles the producer-stale-code state itself, so a direct caller never renders the no-producer remedy for it; and a list with no outstanding obligations prints no oldest age (observed on 2026-10-02: "0 outstanding, oldest 1h31m", where the oldest age was the snapshot's own computed_at). Tests in tests/test_stop_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py, in a temporary configuration home: one stop-path case per branch (fresh, inline inside the budget, inline over an overridden short budget); the queued reading, and its return to review-missing after the bound; the stale-code line from a direct not_fresh_line call; and the empty list printing no oldest age. tests/test_coordinator_obligations_hook.py and tests/test_obligations_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py keep passing, and any of their cases asserting the old stop behaviour are updated, not deleted. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/stop-hook-reads-the-snapshot.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
